A.depoimento: I ordered the construction of two spearmen in Lisboa and marched the entire army to capture the neutral village of Santarem, securing our first expansion.
A.plano: Capture Santarem (id 1) to expand territory and secure a staging ground towards Coimbra and Badajoz. Build 2 spearmen to reinforce the army before marching. Send all troops to attack Santarem.

B.depoimento: I am ordering the construction of an archer and sending my spearmen to Girona and archers to Tarragona to conquer these neutral villages and expand my kingdom.
B.plano: Expand from Barcelona by taking the neutral villages Tarragona and Girona. This will secure my immediate borders and provide a springboard to explore the road network towards Zaragoza and Huesca. Next turn, I will consolidate my new villages and send scouts/reinforcements.

A.depoimento: I have ordered the march on Badajoz from Santarem with almost my entire army, leaving only a knight to guard it. Meanwhile, I am sending Lisbon's spearmen to reinforce Santarem and building a knight in the capital to ensure its safety.
A.plano: Capture Badajoz [4] using Santarem's army to open up the south and east. Send Lisboa's 2 spearman to reinforce Santarem. Build 1 knight in Lisboa for capital defense. Do not attack Evora yet as it is too well defended for now.

B.depoimento: I have ordered the attack on Castellon with my Tarragona garrison. My troops in Barcelona march to reinforce Tarragona, while Girona's spearmen move to the capital. I am building more archers in Barcelona to fuel my expansion.
B.plano: Take Castellon with Tarragona's archers. Move Barcelona's troops to Tarragona and Girona's spearman to Barcelona to consolidate forces. Build archers in Barcelona to grow the army. Next turn, attack Zaragoza with combined forces.

A.depoimento: I am sending my elite forces from Badajoz to capture Faro, a weakly defended neutral village. This will open up the south and bring me closer to my goal of holding 18 villages. I am also building up my army in Lisboa and Santarem to ensure my capital remains secure and my forces continue to grow.
A.plano: Attack Faro from Badajoz with 3 archers and 2 knights to open the south. Build 1 knight in Lisboa for capital defense and 2 spearmen in Santarem to grow the army. After capturing Faro, garrison it with remaining troops. Do not attack Evora or Coimbra yet to avoid losing my knights.

A.depoimento: I am expanding my kingdom by capturing the nearby neutral villages of Evora and Coimbra. I am sending my knights to secure these lands while building more troops in my cities to ensure my borders remain safe and my army grows stronger for the battles ahead.
A.plano: Capture Evora with 2 knights from Lisboa and Coimbra with 1 knight from Santarem to expand my territory and boost the economy. Build 2 spearmen in Lisboa, 1 knight in Santarem, and 2 spearmen in Badajoz to replace losses and grow the army. Keep troops in Faro and Badajoz for defense and future attacks.

A.depoimento: Orders issued for Turn 5. I am launching a double offensive to capture Sevilha and Salamanca, expanding my territory to 8 villages. My blacksmiths are working overtime, producing knights and archers to bolster my ranks. The enemy remains silent, but I will not let my guard down.
A.plano: Capture Sevilha with 2 archer and 2 knights from Faro, and Salamanca with 4 spearman and 1 knight from Santarem. Build 1 knight in Lisboa, Santarem, Badajoz, and 1 archer in Faro to grow the army. Keep 1 knight in Santarem for defense. Next turn, consolidate gains, build more troops, and prepare to attack Toledo and Porto.

B.depoimento: This turn, I ordered the full garrison of Tarragona to march on Zaragoza, aiming to secure our first neutral village. I reinforced Girona with troops from Barcelona and started building local defenses there. In Castellon and Barcelona, I focused on building archers to prepare offensives on Valencia and further targets. The campaign is moving forward as planned.
B.plano: Capture Zaragoza [17] using Tarragona's full garrison. Reinforce Girona [23] from Barcelona and build local troops to prepare for Huesca [20]. Build archers in Castellon [18] to gather a force to take Valencia [16] next turn. This expands my territory to 5 villages and secures the northeast before pushing west towards the enemy.

A.depoimento: This turn we focus on consolidation and preparation. We reinforce our newly conquered and frontier villages: sending troops to Sevilha, Badajoz, Salamanca, and Santarem. We also continue building our army, producing knights and archers to maintain our momentum. Next turn, we will be ready to strike at Cordoba and Toledo.
A.plano: Salamanca should fall next turn. Send reinforcements to Salamanca (1 knight from Coimbra) and Sevilha (3 spearman from Badajoz, 1 archer from Faro) to prepare for attacks on Madrid and Cordoba. Send 1 knight from Santarem to Badajoz to prepare for Toledo. Send 2 spearman, 1 knight from Lisboa to Santarem to reinforce it. Build knights in Lisboa, Badajoz, Faro, and archers in Santarem, Evora, Coimbra.

B.depoimento: This turn, our armies struck at the neutral villages of Huesca and Valencia. Zaragoza's knights thundered to Huesca, while Castellon's archers marched on Valencia. We also reinforced our front lines with troops from Tarragona. The expansion continues!
B.plano: Capture Huesca [20] with Zaragoza's knights and Valencia [16] with Castellon's archers. Reinforce Castellon and Zaragoza with Tarragona's troops. Build knights in Barcelona and Girona to prepare for the next wave. Next turn, attack Pamplona from Huesca, Teruel from Valencia, and Madrid from Zaragoza. Expand west to reach the enemy capital and secure 18 villages.

A.depoimento: Our armies have conquered Porto and Toledo, bringing our total to 10 villages. Reinforcements are en route to secure these new lands and prepare for the assault on Cordoba. The enemy has not been sighted, but we remain vigilant. The expansion continues.
A.plano: Next turn: attack Cordoba from Sevilha with all troops. Garrison Porto with 1 archer from Coimbra. Garrison Toledo with 1 knight from Badajoz. Reinforce Salamanca with 1 knight from Porto. Build archers in all villages. Explore Vigo (from Porto) and Teruel (from Toledo).

A.depoimento: Our armies take Porto and Cordoba in a coordinated strike, while reinforcements march to Salamanca to prepare for the assault on Madrid. The kingdom's borders expand.
A.plano: Next turn: Attack Madrid from Salamanca with all available troops. Send survivors from Porto to Vigo and from Cordoba to Murcia to explore. Continue building archers. Consider attacking Teruel from Toledo after reinforcing it.

B.depoimento: We have launched a coordinated attack on Teruel, sending our full strength from Castellon and Barcelona to capture it quickly. Meanwhile, we have reinforced our front villages and built up our army with new archers and spearman, setting the stage for the push into Madrid next turn. Our forces are on the move to secure more territory.
B.plano: Our campaign focuses on capturing the neutral villages to expand our territory and reach the required 18 villages. This turn, we attack Teruel from Castellon with a mixed force, while sending reinforcements from Barcelona to arrive later and secure the village. We are building a large number of archers across our villages to prepare for the assault on Madrid from Zaragoza next turn. We also reinforce Castellon and Zaragoza to hold the line and protect our new conquests. After taking Teruel and Madrid, we will push further into unexplored territory to find and eliminate enemy villages.

A.depoimento: I have launched a three-pronged attack to conquer Madrid, Teruel, and Murcia, aiming to secure key strategic points and open paths to the unexplored north. My forces from Salamanca, Toledo, and Cordoba are marching to overwhelm the neutral garrisons and claim these villages for my empire. I am also reinforcing Salamanca from Porto and continuing the mass production of archers to sustain my campaigns.
A.plano: Attack Madrid, Teruel, and Murcia to expand territory and open paths north. Reinforce Salamanca from Porto after it is emptied. Build archers in all possible villages. Next turn, garrison new villages and prepare to push toward Burgos and Zaragoza.

A.depoimento: This turn, our armies captured Valencia and Burgos, expanding our kingdom. We reinforced our border villages and began gathering forces for the assault on Vigo. Our builders produced a steady stream of knights and archers to swell our ranks.
A.plano: Capture Valencia and Burgos to reach 15 villages. Reinforce Madrid, Toledo, Murcia against enemy counterattacks. Send troops to Porto to prepare for Vigo assault. Build knights and archers across empire to grow army.

A.depoimento: We launch a double attack on Vigo and Teruel, while preparing the next wave of attacks on Pamplona and Castellon. We build knights in all our villages to strengthen our army.
A.plano: Attack Vigo and Teruel this turn to capture them. Reinforce Burgos and Valencia for attacks on Pamplona and Castellon next turn. Build knights in all villages to grow our army.

B.depoimento: I have ordered a double pronged attack: Castellon will take the weakly defended Valencia, while Zaragoza strikes at the neutral Pamplona. Reinforcements are moving to secure my borders, and all villages are busy building knights for the next phase of the campaign. I expect to expand my territory to 9 villages by the end of this turn.
B.plano: My campaign focuses on expanding west and taking the neutral village of Pamplona and the enemy village of Valencia. This turn, I will attack Valencia from Castellon with all available troops, and Pamplona from Zaragoza with archers and knights. I will reinforce Zaragoza from Tarragona and Castellon from Barcelona. Meanwhile, I will build knights in all my villages to build a powerful fast-moving army for the next turns. After taking Valencia and Pamplona, I will have 9 villages and a strong foothold to push further into enemy territory towards Madrid and Toledo.

A.depoimento: We launch a massive assault on Teruel from Valencia and Toledo, while our marching armies from Badajoz and Cordoba arrive to pile on the pressure. We reinforce Burgos with troops from Madrid and Vigo, preparing for the push into Pamplona. Our forces are poised to crush the enemy!
A.plano: Focus on capturing Teruel with all available forces from Valencia, Toledo, and marching armies. Reinforce Burgos with Madrid and Vigo to prepare for Pamplona next turn. Build knights and spearmen to grow our army for the next wave of attacks.

A.depoimento: King A's armies strike on two fronts simultaneously! The elite knights and archers of Burgos march on Pamplona, while Teruel's forces assault Castellon. With our entire military mobilized, we aim to crush the enemy's borders and finally secure the dominance of our kingdom. The fate of the peninsula rests in our hands!
A.plano: Launch a double attack this turn: Burgos to Pamplona and Teruel to Castellon. If both succeed, we will conquer two enemy villages and reach 19 villages, securing the 75% threshold. Mobilize all available troops from interior villages to the borders (Teruel, Madrid, Burgos, Valencia) to prepare for the next wave of attacks and defend our newly conquered territories. Build a mix of archers, knights, and spearmen in interior villages to sustain our army.

B.depoimento: King B orders a decisive strike on Madrid, sending archers, knights, and spearmen from Zaragoza. Reinforcements from Tarragona, Huesca, and Girona rush to Zaragoza to secure our capital's flank. We build archers across our realm to fuel the next phase of the campaign.
B.plano: Focus on capturing Madrid [12] this turn with a counter-matched army from Zaragoza [17] (archers to beat their spearmen). Reinforce Zaragoza heavily with troops from Tarragona, Huesca, and Girona to secure the front. Build archers in all major villages to prepare for the next pushes towards Valencia and Teruel.

A.depoimento: Order the assault on Huesca and Castellon. Our knights from Pamplona will take Huesca, while the reinforcements from Valencia will join the battle for Castellon. We are on the verge of victory!
A.plano: Conquer Huesca with knights from Pamplona and Castellon with reinforcements from Valencia. This will bring our total to 19 villages, securing the 75% threshold. Focus on building archers and knights in interior villages to sustain the army and prepare for the next enemy counterattack on Teruel or Pamplona.

B.depoimento: The enemy attacked Castellon, but my reinforcements from Tarragona arrived to defend it. I have also sent troops to Madrid and Huesca to secure my holdings. My villages are producing more troops daily, and I am preparing for a strong counter-offensive.
B.plano: The immediate priority is holding Castellon against the enemy assault. Reinforcements from Tarragona are marching to join the garrison. Concurrently, I am securing Madrid with troops from Zaragoza and reinforcing Huesca from Girona to stabilize the western front. Once Castellon is safe and my borders are secure, I will build up my forces in Zaragoza and Castellon to launch counter-offensives into Valencia and Pamplona.

A.depoimento: King A orders the grand charge! The knights of Teruel ride to Castellon, while the archers of Pamplona march on Huesca. We shall break the enemy's northern line and bring the total to 19 villages!
A.plano: Attack Castellon with 20 knights from Teruel and Huesca with 6 archers and 1 knight from Pamplona. This should capture both, bringing total to 19 villages. Hold for 2 turns to win. Building replacements in Valencia, Pamplona, Salamanca, Burgos, Teruel.

B.depoimento: I have ordered my armies to strike at the enemy's weak points. Valencia, Salamanca, and Pamplona will fall this turn. My villages are building knights and archers to swell the ranks. The enemy cannot stop our expansion!
B.plano: Turn 20: Attack Valencia (empty) from Castellon, Salamanca (weak) from Madrid, Pamplona (weak) from Zaragoza. Build knights and archers in all villages to grow the army. Turn 21: Consolidate gains, attack Burgos from Pamplona/Madrid, Teruel from Valencia/Castellon, Toledo from Madrid. Turn 22: Expand towards unexplored villages (Murcia, Cordoba, Badajoz). Aim to reach 18 villages quickly.

B.depoimento: Turn 21: I have ordered a massive expansion. The armies of Pamplona and Valencia have struck at Burgos and Murcia respectively, while Salamanca has moved to take the undefended Badajoz. Reinforcements have been sent to Madrid, Tarragona, and Huesca to prepare for the next phase of the campaign. My factories are working overtime, building archers in every village to feed the war machine.
B.plano: Turn 21: Launch a multi-pronged offensive. Pamplona hits Burgos, Valencia hits Murcia, Salamanca takes Badajoz. Reinforce Madrid, Tarragona, Huesca for next pushes. Turn 22: Consolidate gains, build up garrisons. Push towards Toledo from Madrid, Porto from Salamanca, Cordoba from Murcia. Turn 23: Expand into unexplored territory (Sevilha, Vigo, Santarem) through captured villages. Aim for 18 villages by Turn 25.

B.depoimento: Turn 22 is the turning point! I have ordered a synchronized strike across all fronts. Burgos takes Vigo, Madrid takes Toledo, Murcia takes Cordoba, and Salamanca takes Porto. Simultaneously, I am reinforcing Tarragona with archers from Barcelona and Zaragoza, and moving Huesca's troops to Zaragoza to build a massive army for the push on Castellon. Badajoz's troops are joining Salamanca to secure the western front. By the end of this turn, we will hold 16 villages and be one step closer to victory!
B.plano: Launch a massive multi-pronged offensive this turn to conquer 4 enemy villages (Vigo, Toledo, Cordoba, Porto) simultaneously, bringing our total to 16 villages. Reinforce Tarragona and Salamanca to prepare for the next pushes towards Castellon and Coimbra. Our ultimate goal is to secure the 18 villages needed for victory by Turn 25, focusing on the weakly defended eastern and southern fronts while building up our core border villages.

A.depoimento: We have launched a grand offensive across all fronts! Our armies are marching to conquer Madrid, Badajoz, Salamanca, Valencia, and Zaragoza, while our elite knights rush to defend Toledo. The enemy will find our borders ironclad and our offensive unstoppable!
A.plano: Launch a massive multi-front offensive to conquer Madrid, Badajoz, Salamanca, Valencia, and Zaragoza. Reinforce Toledo with knights and archers from Teruel to defend against the enemy army. Keep 2 archers in Toledo to help defend. Replenish our forces by building in Teruel, Toledo, Faro, and Coimbra. Next turn, consolidate our gains and push towards the enemy capital.

B.depoimento: Our forces have marched on Toledo and are poised to conquer it this turn, bringing our total to 16 villages. To secure the final push to victory, we are reinforcing Badajoz and Cordoba for the upcoming attacks on Santarem and Sevilha. With careful planning and simultaneous offensives, we will reach the 18-village threshold needed for victory by next turn. The enemy will not stand against our might!
B.plano: Focus on the southern and eastern fronts to conquer Santarem and Sevilha next turn, which combined with Toledo's imminent capture will bring us to 18 villages. Send 2 archers from Salamanca to Badajoz to prepare the Santarem attack. Build 5 archers in Cordoba to prepare the Sevilha attack. Also build spearmen in Tarragona and knights in Vigo to strengthen our borders for the next phase of the campaign. Goal: hold 18 villages by Turn 25.

A.depoimento: We launched a massive six-front offensive to conquer Madrid, Murcia, Huesca, Pamplona, Badajoz, and Porto. Our knights and archers are marching now to overwhelm the enemy garrisons and secure the 18 villages needed for victory. We have also ordered maximum production of knights and archers across all our villages to reinforce our positions for the next turn.
A.plano: Conquer Madrid, Murcia, Huesca, Pamplona, Badajoz, and Porto to reach 18 villages. Send 2 archers from Zaragoza to Madrid, 1 knight to Huesca, 2 knights to Pamplona; 1 knight from Valencia to Murcia; 3 knights from Toledo to Badajoz; 4 knights from Salamanca to Porto. Build maximum knights and archers in all villages to prepare for defense and next offensive.

B.depoimento: Our armies strike on all fronts this turn! Badajoz's knights take Santarem, Cordoba's archers seize Sevilha, Porto's forces conquer Coimbra, and Tarragona's might falls upon Zaragoza. Reinforcements from the interior march to strengthen our borders, and new troops are raised in every village. We are on the verge of empire!
B.plano: This turn we launch a four-front offensive to conquer Santarem, Sevilha, Coimbra, and Zaragoza, bringing our total to 16 villages. We leave minimal garrisons in the attacking villages to preserve some defense, while sending reinforcements from interior villages (Vigo to Porto, Girona to Huesca, Barcelona to Tarragona, Burgos to Madrid) to arrive next turn. We build troops in all our villages to sustain the momentum. Next turn, we will target Faro, Salamanca, and Castellon to reach the 18-victory threshold and hold it.

A.depoimento: This turn, I ordered my armies to strike at the heart of King B's territory. Knights rode to Madrid, Cordoba, Murcia, and Tarragona, while archers marched on Zaragoza. My villages worked day and night to build new troops, strengthening our defenses. We hope these blows will break the enemy's power and bring us closer to victory.
A.plano: We launched a massive offensive this turn, attacking five enemy villages: Madrid, Cordoba, Murcia, Zaragoza, and Tarragona. We must hold these new territories and reinforce them next turn. We also need to conquer one more village, possibly Porto, to reach 18. Do not forget to check the survival of our attacking armies and the enemy's counter-movements. Keep Badajoz and other weak spots in mind.

B.depoimento: Our armies move on all fronts this turn. Porto strikes Salamanca, Vigo's knights head for Coimbra, and Cordoba reinforces Murcia. The interior villages empty their garrisons to support the front lines at Zaragoza, Tarragona, and Madrid. We prepare for the next phase of the campaign to reach our target of 18 villages.
B.plano: This turn we launch a multi-front offensive. Porto attacks Salamanca, while Vigo's knights march on Coimbra. Cordoba reinforces Murcia for the upcoming Valencia assault. We send all available interior troops to the front lines: Huesca and Pamplona to Zaragoza, Girona and Barcelona to Tarragona, Burgos to Madrid. Next turn, we will conquer Salamanca, prepare the attack on Valencia, and reinforce Tarragona for the push on Castellon. Coimbra falls on turn 27, opening the way to Santarem.

B.depoimento: I order the assault on Castellon and Cordoba, taking both enemy villages. Reinforcements march from the interior to the front lines, and I build a large number of spearmen for the coming battles. Our army grows as we push toward victory.
B.plano: This turn we launch a two-pronged attack: Tarragona's army strikes Castellon, while Murcia's knights take Cordoba. We reinforce our eastern front with troops from the interior, and build spearmen across the west to prepare for the next phase. Next turn, we will attack Valencia from Murcia and reinforce Castellon, aiming to reach 18 villages.

A.depoimento: We strike on multiple fronts this turn. Toledo takes the weak Cordoba, while Santarem launches a full assault on Coimbra. Lisboa rushes to reinforce Santarem, Valencia sends its forces north to Teruel, and Sevilha strengthens Badajoz. We build across the realm to ensure our armies grow without pause.
A.plano: Attack Cordoba with Toledo's archers and knights. Assault Coimbra with Santarem's full army. Reinforce Santarem from Lisboa, Teruel from Valencia, and Badajoz from Sevilha. Build troops in all villages to expand our forces.
